properties.decision:
Anthony asked 2026-07-31 whether a "start here" file or node should tell a newly-cloned agent what it needs to pick up where the last person left off — offered explicitly as an idea to explore, with the observation that reflow2 often already has something. It does, and the answer is: BUILD THE VIEW, NOT THE DOCUMENT.

NO START-HERE FILE. Two recorded positions already forbid it, and neither is a stretch. `req:session-memory-in-graph`: "a summary written at the end is the one a busy session never gets to, and an end-of-session digest is a retelling rather than a record." And `dec:what-lives-where`'s whole storyflow lesson is prose-you-navigate losing to graph-you-query. A START-HERE.md is `dev_storyflow` in miniature — it would go stale, and STALENESS IN AN ORIENTATION DOCUMENT IS THE WORST PLACE FOR IT, because it is the first thing read and the reader has nothing yet to check it against.

THE NEED IS REAL AND MOSTLY ALREADY DESIGNED. Three planned capabilities cover it between them: `cap:what-next` (which of the agreed things to do now, ranked so an unmade decision outranks the work waiting on it), `cap:onboarding` (where does a new piece of work belong, for someone who did not build the system), and `cap:session-memory` (what the last session learned, queryable rather than narrated). None needs a document; all three are projections, which is what `dec:views-are-projections` already says every view is.

WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING, and it belongs in `cap:what-next` rather than in a new thing: WHICH FEW DECISIONS SHAPE EVERYTHING ELSE. Neither what-next nor where-am-i answers it today, and it is what a newcomer actually needs — not the task list, but the handful of choices that explain why the rest looks as it does.

EVIDENCE AGAINST URGENCY, recorded because it is the kind of thing that otherwise gets built on a feeling. `where-am-i` DID orient a fresh agent on this design earlier the same day: 627 nodes, roughly six calls, using `scan_nodes` with `brief: true` and reading six Decisions in full. It scales today because reads are bounded (`cap:bounded-reads`). The concern that it stops working is a FORECAST, not yet an observation — worth watching rather than pre-solving, and worth re-measuring when the answer changes rather than assuming it has.

SO THE ORDER IS: build `cap:what-next`, whose blocker has already cleared, and add the shaping-decisions section to it. Do not add a fourth thing beside three planned ones that already answer the question.
properties.name: No START-HERE document — orientation is a projection, and writing it down would be dev_storyflow in miniature
properties.rationale:
Taken on the recommendation rather than the request, which is the point worth noting: the question was "should we write a start-here document", and the honest answer was that the artefact would work against the reason the project exists. Anthony's own framing left room for that — "maybe this isn't needed because an agent using reflow2 can already quickly know what a project is about" — and the measurement supports it.

The more useful outcome was not the answer but what looking produced: `cap:what-next` states a prerequisite that has since been met, and nothing surfaced it. A capability that records its own blocking condition in prose has written a trigger that nothing fires. That is the same shape as every other declared-but-unread property this project keeps finding, and it is the argument for the shaping-decisions section being a COMPUTATION rather than another paragraph.

The in-degree caveat is kept deliberately. The first version of the idea looked convincing because the top three results were genuinely load-bearing; the top result was not, and reporting the idea without that would have been reporting a demo rather than a measurement.
